_comment: Storyboard for the Grade 4 Science unit lecture film, Lesson 10 Circuits and Switches. Rendered by tools/create-ehel-unit-lecture.js. See lecture-video/BRIEF.md. Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow LESSON['lecture'] in order (one loop; a switch; brighter and dimmer; conductors and insulators; today), with the lesson's safety rules as their own chapter because 4TWSp.05 is taught in two of its steps. The pictures are the lesson's own: ART.kit.circuitSvg (the circuit the child builds, with its gap), ART.kit.seriesSvg (the seriesCircuit sim: cells, lamps and the switch) and the conductor sim's own circuit-with-a-gap, with the lesson's eight test materials.
title: Circuits and Switches
subtitle: Grade 4 Science
objectives: Know that an electrical device will not work if there is a break in the circuit.
Describe how a simple switch is used to open and close a circuit.
Describe how changing the number or type of components in a series circuit can make a lamp brighter or dimmer.
Know some materials are good electrical conductors, especially metals, and some are good electrical insulators.
Identify risks and explain how to stay safe during practical work.
Choose equipment from a provided selection and use it appropriately.
Collect and record observations and/or measurements in tables and diagrams.

beats.say: Electricity flows round a loop. Break the loop anywhere, and it stops.
A cell pushes it round. A switch lets you stop it when you want.
A cell, two wires and a lamp make one loop: a series circuit.
The wire runs from the cell to the lamp, and back to the cell.
The loop is complete. Electricity flows, and the lamp lights.
Now a wire comes loose. That gap is a break in the circuit.
Nothing can flow, so the lamp goes out. One break stops it all.
A switch is a break you control. Inside are two metal contacts.
Closed, the contacts touch. The loop is complete and the lamp lights.
Open, there is a gap between them. Nothing flows, and the lamp is dark.
The cell is still full. It is the path that is broken.
A doorbell button is a switch. It closes only while you press it.
Let go, and it springs open again. The bell stops.
Cells push the electricity round the loop. One cell, one lamp.
Add a second cell. The push is bigger, so the lamp is brighter.
Now add a second lamp. The same push is shared between the two.
A shared push means each lamp is dimmer than it was before.
More cells: brighter. More lamps: dimmer. Open the switch: off.
Leave a gap in the loop. Put a material in that gap and test it.
A conductor lets electricity through, so the lamp lights up.
Copper wire, a steel key, a coin: metals are the best conductors.
An insulator does not let it through. Plastic, rubber, wood, glass.
A shiny plastic lid is an insulator. It is the metal that conducts.
That is why a wire is copper inside and plastic outside.
Build your circuit with cells only. Never the plug socket.
A cell gives a small, safe push. Mains electricity can kill.
Water carries electricity. Dry your hands before you touch a switch.
If a wire gets hot, open the switch and tell a grown-up.
Today you add cells and lamps, and watch the light change.
You open and close the switch, then test eight materials in the gap.
Write each one in a table: conductor, or insulator.
And choose the right equipment: a cell for brighter, never more wire.
One loop, all the way round. A break anywhere stops everything.
A switch opens and closes a gap. More cells, brighter. More lamps, dimmer.
Metals conduct. Plastic, rubber, wood and glass insulate.
